**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity, confidence 0.86)**

**What I found.** Despite the planner's expectation that renewal mechanics were absent, they are in fact buried in Section 13 (TERM OF AGREEMENT), which the outline mis-assigns to the § 12 INDEMNITY section — so a section-level review of `sec-5` alone would have missed it.

**Assessment against the rule:**

| Parameter | Preferred | Document | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Renewal term | 12 months | "successive one year periods" | ✅ compliant |
| Non-renewal notice | ≤ 30 days | "thirty (30) days prior" | ✅ compliant |
| Vendor reminder | 60 days pre-renewal | none | ❌ missing |
| Uplift cap | lesser of CPI / 3% | none | ❌ missing |

The notice window and term length are already at our preferred position, and the opt-out is mutual — no need to touch either, so no walk-away trigger. The gap is pricing predictability: Section 6 (p0047) freezes Hosting Services costs for only "a period of one year from the date of this Agreement," which expires precisely when the first automatic renewal begins. After that, renewal pricing is entirely uncapped, and with a 30-day opt-out we could be notified of an increase with little runway to migrate. The most-favored-rates language in p0047 is relative, not absolute, so it constrains discrimination but not escalation.

**Edit made.** A single `replace` op on p0078 appending two sentences after the existing notice language: a 60-day written renewal reminder from TrueLink, and a renewal fee cap at the lesser of CPI-over-12-months and 3%. Validated `ok:true`; the diff confirms the insertion lands cleanly between the notice sentence and the existing wind-down provisions, leaving all surrounding text intact. The comment offers the fallback 5% flat cap to give the counterparty a landing zone without conceding it upfront.
